title: Anagram Checker
description: Write a Java method that checks if two given strings are anagrams of each other. An anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase. Your check should be case-insensitive and should only consider alphabetic characters, ignoring spaces and punctuation.

title: Recursive Factorial
description:
Write a recursive Java method to calculate the factorial of a non-negative integer N. The factorial of a number is the product of all positive integers up to that number.

Base Case: factorial(0) = 1.
Recursive Relation: factorial(N) = N * factorial(N-1) for N > 0.

title: Rotate Array Right by K Positions
description: Write a Java method that rotates an array of integers to the right by a specified number of positions, `k`. In a right rotation, each element of the array is shifted one unit to the right, and the last element of the array becomes the first element.

title: Implement Bubble Sort
description: Write a Java method to sort an array of integers using the Bubble Sort algorithm. Bubble sort repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. The pass through the list is repeated until the list is sorted.

title: Print a Hollow Diamond Pattern
description: Given an odd integer N, write a Java program that prints a hollow diamond pattern of stars (*). The diamond should have N rows and N columns at its widest point.

title: Singly Linked List Deletion
description:
Your task is to implement the deletion method for a Singly Linked List from scratch. You will need to create a `Node` class and a `SinglyLinkedList` class. Implement the following method:

`deleteNode(int data)`: Deletes the first node that contains the given data. Handle edge cases like deleting the head or a node from an empty list.

title: Doubly Linked List Insertion
description:
Your task is to implement the insertion method for a Doubly Linked List from scratch. You will need a `Node` class (with `next` and `prev` pointers) and a `DoublyLinkedList` class. Implement the following method:

`insertAtPosition(int data, int position)`: Inserts a new node with the given data at the specified position (0-indexed). Handle edge cases like inserting at the head, tail, or into an empty list.
